launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.description: The Saint Louis Zoo offers free general admission and full-day animal exhibits; its north and south lots are paid and cashless, while limited park street spaces are free.
Saint Louis Art Museum has free general admission above the Grand Basin, with separately ticketed exhibitions, independent hours, free curb parking and a paid garage.
Missouri History Museum provides free exhibits at the park's north edge near MetroLink and trolley connections, with independent opening and event hours.
Saint Louis Science Center offers free general admission at the southeast edge, while parking, OMNIMAX, special exhibitions and selected activities cost separately.
The Muny is a seasonal outdoor musical theater with free seats at the rear and separately ticketed reserved seating; show nights reshape traffic and parking.
Grand Basin and Art Hill form the park's landmark lake-and-lawn view below the Art Museum, with paved walks, boating views and popular winter sledding.
The Jewel Box is a historic Art Deco greenhouse with floral displays and a reflecting pool; interior access, admission and event closures follow a separate schedule.
The free 17-acre Nature Playscape uses water, sand, logs, rocks and native landscapes for open-ended play; pets and bicycles remain outside the play zones.

launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.description: The 630-foot stainless-steel Gateway Arch is viewed freely from the grounds; entering the underground complex requires the west entrance and security screening.
The free underground museum interprets Indigenous, colonial, expansion, migration and civil-rights histories and can be visited without buying a tram ticket.
The ticketed tram uses compact enclosed capsules to reach the observation deck; advance reservations are recommended and the experience is not wheelchair accessible.
The restored Old Courthouse has free exhibits and historic courtrooms, including interpretation of the Dred and Harriet Scott cases, during separate daily hours.
Luther Ely Smith Square creates the paved western approach between the Old Courthouse and Arch entrance, crossing downtown streets before the security checkpoint.
The landscaped Arch Grounds are free from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. with paved accessible paths, lawns and river views but limited shade near midday.
Riverboat cruises board at the Mississippi levee on separately ticketed seasonal schedules; river stage, weather and private events can alter departures.
Leonor K. Sullivan Boulevard follows the river below the Arch; reach it by the Grand Staircase or longer ramps and check flooding or event closures before descending.

launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.description: Muckerman Children's Fountain is the seasonal central splash pad beside Central Playground, generally operating 10 a.m.-7 p.m. weather and maintenance permitting.
Central Playground sits near the Roman Pavilion and splash pad, making this the most convenient family arrival zone for conventional play and water features.
Nee Kee Nee is a nature-based East Stream playscape with logs, stones, water and climbing elements, generally running timed water cycles from 10 a.m.-4 p.m.
Piper Palm House is a historic conservatory-style event building with palm displays; private rentals and programs mean interior access is not guaranteed.
The Victorian Music Stand anchors concerts and community gatherings on a central lawn; event setup can restrict nearby paths and parking.
The ornate Turkish Pavilion is a reservable picnic and event shelter; a reservation may limit use even while surrounding park paths remain open.
Tower Grove Farmers' Market operates on scheduled seasonal market days with food, produce, crowds and changing vendor layouts rather than daily park hours.
East Stream is the restored water landscape around Nee Kee Nee, intended for supervised nature play during operating cycles rather than unsupervised swimming.

launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.description: The Children's Spray Plaza is Citygarden's only water feature designed for public play, generally open 10 a.m.-6 p.m. from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day.
Split Basin is a black-granite and limestone waterfall-inspired landscape for viewing and listening; swimming and wading are prohibited.
Voyager Pool is a reflecting pool surrounding Jean-Michel Folon's Voyage; it is an artwork setting, not a public wading pool.
Tom Claassen's Untitled (Two Rabbits) is a pair of oversized bronze animals viewed from garden paths; visitors should not climb the sculpture.
Jim Dine's Big White Gloves, Big Four Wheels is a monumental Pinocchio figure and one of the garden's easiest family landmarks to locate.
Igor Mitoraj's Eros Bendato is a monumental reclining head within the sculpture landscape, viewed from surrounding paved routes.
Dance Chimes create a sound-making interactive surface within the garden; use gently and supervise children around other visitors and wet surfaces.
The terrace and lawns provide seating, shade and downtown views between sculpture zones; food service and private programming can change available space.

launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.description: The Climatron is a geodesic conservatory containing a warm, humid tropical rainforest collection; indoor temperature, narrow paths and maintenance closures affect visits.
Seiwa-en is a 14-acre Japanese strolling garden with lake, islands, bridges and carefully framed views; remain on paths and do not feed wildlife unless expressly permitted.
The seasonal Children's Garden adds caves, slides, treehouse, wetlands and a Memorial Day-Labor Day splash pad with separate child admission and caregiver rules.
The Chinese Garden is a compact walled landscape of architecture, stone, water and plants intended for quiet viewing from maintained paths.
Tower Grove House is Henry Shaw's historic country home with seasonal guided access; its historic structure is not wheelchair or stroller accessible.
Linnean House is one of the oldest continuously operated public greenhouses west of the Mississippi, with seasonal camellias and independent temporary closures.
Brookings Exploration Center provides year-round indoor family exhibits, maker activities and a nearby calming room, all included with general Garden admission.
Kemper Center combines home-gardening displays, demonstration beds, library resources and visitor services in an accessible complex at the Garden's western side.

launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.description: Alexander Liberman's The Way is a monumental red steel composition on the main lawn and one of Laumeier's defining landmarks; do not climb it.
Tony Tasset's giant realistic Eye sits in the outdoor collection and is viewed from the lawn and Central Pathway without touching or climbing.
Donald Lipski's Ball? Ball! Wall? Wall! combines a large sphere and architectural form near the central outdoor gallery; follow the artwork's interaction label.
Aronson Fine Arts Center provides free changing exhibitions, visitor help, restrooms and wheelchair checkout during shorter Thursday-Sunday seasonal hours.
The 0.77-mile Art Hike Trail begins near the lower entrance and follows natural woodland terrain past sculpture, requiring about 45 minutes under ordinary conditions.
The 0.64-mile paved Central Pathway links lower and west entrances, but its natural grades are steeper than ADA standards despite the hard surface.
Way Field is the broad lawn around The Way with sculpture views, picnic space and accessible restrooms; major events can fully close or occupy it.
The Children's Sculpture Garden includes artful play elements with specific interaction rules; supervise children and follow each object label before touching or climbing.

launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.description: Elk Range Drive is the one-way vehicle route through elk habitat; remain in the vehicle, drive slowly and never stop in a way that blocks other visitors.
The bison range places visitors near powerful free-ranging animals from inside a vehicle; windows, doors and food should remain controlled at all times.
White Bison Trail is a roughly three-mile wooded natural-surface loop with hills, roots and mud, offering wildlife habitat views without guaranteed sightings.
The visitor information area provides orientation, restrooms and current wildlife or closure guidance during posted access, near the reservoir and trail connections.
Lone Elk Reservoir provides waterfowl, fishing and quiet picnic views under posted rules; it is not a swimming destination and shoreline conditions vary.
Elk Hollow is a reservable picnic shelter separated from animal travel lanes; reservations, access and restroom availability should be checked before group visits.
Elk observation opportunities occur throughout the managed drive rather than at one guaranteed viewing pen; sightings shift with weather, season and animal behavior.
Bison are viewed from designated road and pull-off areas only; never leave the vehicle or approach an animal to improve a photograph.

launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.description: The 320-acre Creve Coeur Lake supports paddling, sailing and fishing under posted rules; ordinary swimming is not allowed and water conditions can close access.
The roughly 3.8-mile paved Lakeview Loop is a flat shared route around the lake with substantial sun exposure, busy weekend traffic and several shoreline access points.
Sailboat Cove is the primary lower-lake arrival for boating, rentals, shelters and shoreline activity; parking fills quickly during races and warm weekends.
Mallard Lake is a smaller wetland and fishing destination connected to the larger trail system, with quieter habitat and flood-sensitive approaches.
Creve Coeur Connector Trail climbs from the lake system toward regional greenway and Missouri River connections, adding distance and grade beyond the lake loop.
The marked water trail supports paddlers on the lake under current launch, wind and safety rules; rentals and life-jacket requirements apply independently.
The disc-golf course occupies a separate upper-park recreation area; watch for flying discs and do not use active fairways as picnic or play space.
The seasonal splash pad and nearby playground provide free family play away from lake water; confirm operation, exact parking and restroom availability before visiting.
